Subject: SlateBio — context budget & prefetch strategy for Dedicated commitment

Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call, I pulled together a concise recommendation for how to map SlateBio's clinical-document workload (avg. 6k tokens/session, 95th 28k; interactive assistant spikes to 120k) into a Dedicated deployment that balances latency, predictable throughput, and unit cost. The attached matrix summarizes memory pressure per model variant and three pragmatic deployment patterns.

Key takeaways up front:
- If you need sub-200ms token tail latency for interactive sessions at peak, we recommend keeping KV resident on GPU and using an 8-bit quantized variant with pinned GPU capacity. That increases GPU count but preserves latency.
- If 300–500ms tail latency is acceptable, a hybrid approach (windowed KV + host-prefetch) with aggressive quantization (4/8-bit mixed) reduces GPU count by ~30% at modest latency cost.
- We also modeled a spill-to-host strategy for long-prompt offload (for the rare 120k sessions) that lowers reserved GPU footprint but adds occasional 100–300ms spikes during prefetch.

Attached: slate_memory_matrix.xlsx (detailed per-model footprint), slate_prefetch_playbook.pdf (ops notes), and a preliminary quote.

Ask: can you confirm which SLAs matter most for the initial 12-month commitment (tail latency at p99, steady throughput, or strict monthly cost cap)? That will let us pick the right mix of pinned GPUs vs. hybrid pooling.

Elena — great questions. Looping Marcus (Inference Eng) for the micro-benchmarks and Soojin (Product) for how the offering maps to Dedicated SKUs and compliance controls. Answers below plus a compact table in the attached sheet.

1) Host-prefetch frequency (estimates for SlateBio profile)
- Typical session (6k avg): 0% prefetch; everything stays in LRU under our cache policy.
- 95th (28k): ~12–18% of sessions will require incremental KV fetches beyond the pinned prefix (small extra latency window 40–120ms when prefetch overlaps generation).
- Extreme spike (120k): ~1–2% of sessions will require multi-stage prefetch and temporary disk spill; expect 150–350ms added latency during the join/fetch window.

These figures assume the "prefetch-window" setting at 32k tokens and a KV-reserve per-pod of ~6–8GB for the base model. See slate_memory_matrix.xlsx, column 'prefetch_prob'.

2) Quantization impact on quality and footprint
- 8-bit (INT8/quantized float): ~35–45% reduction in model activation memory vs FP16; negligible quality delta for the assistant models after our calibration. Good middle ground for sub-200ms p99.
- 4-bit (LLM-int4 / grouped quant): ~60–70% reduction in activation memory but increased per-token CPU/GPU post-processing. Expect a measurable quality drop on some clinical summarization prompts. For SlateBio's closed-domain models, we saw a ~3–7% delta on rouge/recall in our evals — acceptable for research workloads but we don't recommend for clinical release.

3) Compliance for spill/prefetch
- Hybrid mode supports KMS-wrapped encryption for in-flight and at-rest on host spill, and keys live in the customer's KMS in Private and Dedicated options. We will provide an architecture diagram and a SOC2 control mapping in the playbook (slate_prefetch_playbook.pdf).

Recommended options (short):
A) Low-latency, higher-commit: Pinned 80GB GPUs with INT8 quantized runtime, KV fully resident on GPU. Target p99 token latency <200ms. Est. reserved pods: 8 pods; monthly commitment: ~$XXXk.
B) Cost-first, hybrid: 40GB nodes with dynamic prefetch window (32k) and mixed 4/8-bit quant. Acceptable p99 ~350ms, saves ~30% on committed GPU spend. Est. reserved pods: 6 pods; monthly commitment: ~$YYYk.
C) On-demand+spill: Minimal reserved footprint, host-prefetch + spill to NVMe for archival prompts. Lowest monthly commit but larger latency variance.

Marcus: attaching the microbench table and end-to-end mem breakdown. Can you call out any thermal / scheduling constraints if SlateBio picks option B?

Sooj: can you add the SKU mapping and a short note on how this maps to the Dedicated contract language (burst caps, headroom, SLA exceptions) so Elena can pass to procurement?

Thanks — aiming to have a short recommendation pack for procurement by EOD Friday.

Best,
Naomi
